findings: Rate limit key is req.ip, not the API key as documented ('Each API key is limited to 100 requests per minute') — this directly explains the reported symptom: a shared-office customer behind NAT/a single egress IP has all users' requests pooled into one bucket, exhausting the limit far faster than the doc implies.

The bucket count is never reset or windowed by time — there is no timestamp, timer, or sliding/fixed window logic of any kind, so the limit is not 'per minute' as documented; it's a lifetime (or until-process-restart) cumulative counter, making the effective limit far stricter than advertised.

No Retry-After header (or any header) is ever produced by checkLimit — the function only returns {limited: true}, so the documented 'returns HTTP 429 ... with a Retry-After header indicating when to retry' is not implemented anywhere in the shown code.
No HTTP status code handling is shown/implemented — checkLimit returns a boolean-ish object, not an actual 429 response; nothing in the snippet maps limited:true to HTTP 429.
The buckets Map is never pruned or expired, so it grows unboundedly (one entry per distinct IP forever) — a memory leak, and also the mechanism by which counts never decay back down.

Because there's no reset, once any client (or shared IP) crosses 100 total requests, it is permanently locked out with no path to recovery short of a server restart, contradicting the documented recoverable 'per minute' limit.
